title: Bluedip: fill a restaurant's quiet hours
about: A founder describes Bluedip, an app that predicts a restaurant's footfall and revenue hour by hour and estimates what an offer will really do before the owner runs it. Cynqra builds the team the idea needs: a Data Scientist for the models, a Restaurant Revenue Management Specialist, a CFO, a Market Analyst, a Legal and Compliance Advisor, a Project Manager, a CTO and an engineer. They work at the same time; the platform backtests the forecast (its first version fails), the engineer asks the Specialist instead of guessing, the CEO decides one rule on discounts, and the app goes live. The owner's own example, 50% off for 15 customers from 1 to 4 pm, turns out to raise revenue and lose money; Bluedip recommends the offer that earns it.
note: Prepared script for demo mode. Every word a worker says in demo mode comes from this file, and the product shows that. The models and the app in files/ are real: they are tested, backtested and deployed for real.
messy: I want to build Bluedip, an app that helps restaurant owners fill their quiet hours. It should predict footfall and revenue for breakfast, lunch and dinner in real time, recommend offers for the slow periods, and let an owner create a limited-time offer, like 50% off for at most 15 customers between 1 PM and 4 PM, and see how many customers it will bring and what it does to revenue. First release for restaurant owners only: no diner app and no payments.

objective.product: Bluedip: an app that helps restaurant owners fill their quiet hours with offers that earn money
objective.target_customer: Owners of independent restaurants and small chains in Indian cities
objective.primary_outcome: Owners see expected footfall and revenue for every hour and meal, and run offers that fill quiet hours without losing margin
objective.business_outcome: Restaurants pay a monthly subscription because Bluedip adds more margin than it costs
objective.success_criteria: A live app that predicts footfall and revenue by hour and estimates the customers, revenue and margin an offer brings, and a checked business plan
objective.constraints: No diner-facing app or payments in the first release; every estimate shows the assumptions behind it
objective.priorities: Honest estimates first, then recommendations for each meal, then growth

outcomes: Owners see their day's footfall and revenue before it happens

workforce.summary: A company built on prediction, not only an app. A Data Scientist owns the footfall and offer models; a Restaurant Revenue Management Specialist, because whether a discount earns money is this company's field; a CFO, a Market Analyst and a Legal and Compliance Advisor for the business foundation; a Business Lead runs the business side for the founder; a Project Manager coordinates; a CTO and one engineer build and release the owner's app. No Security Expert yet: release 1 holds no diner data and takes no payments.

t_08.problem: Owners will set their own discounts. A deep one can fill the room and still lose money, because customers who would have come anyway pay less too; an app that lets that happen without saying so loses the owner's trust.
t_08.recommendation: No offer deeper than 50%, and none that takes the bill below its food cost. Every offer shows its margin change after food cost before it is created, and a better offer when there is one.
t_08.cost: some owners will want deeper discounts than Bluedip allows
t_08.what_would_change_this: Pilot results showing offers deeper than 50% adding margin in some restaurants.
